DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World (Gabon page, last modified January 2025) confirms that Gabon's Personal Data Protection Act (Act No. 001/2011, as amended by Act No. 025/2023 of 9 July 2023) imposes mandatory breach notification: Article 142 requires data controllers to notify the data protection authority (APDPVP) without delay, and Articles 145-146 require notification to affected individuals where a breach poses a high risk to their rights. As payment service providers are data controllers processing personal (including payment) data, this general obligation applies to them. Gabon's Cybersecurity Law No. 027/2023 (Article 25) separately requires public administrations to report cybersecurity incidents to the competent authority. No payment-sector-specific breach notification regulation was found, but the general Data Protection Act obligation is mandatory and enforceable, supporting a score of 3 (Mandatory) rather than 0. revised_comments: Gabon's Personal Data Protection Act (Act No. 001/2011, as amended by Act No. 025/2023 of 9 July 2023) makes breach notification mandatory. Under Article 142, data controllers - which include payment service providers processing personal data - must notify the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Authority (APDPVP) without delay of any data breach, providing details of its nature, the categories and approximate number of persons affected, remedial measures taken or planned, and contact details of the Data Protection Officer. Where a breach is likely to pose a high risk to data subjects' rights and freedoms, Articles 145-146 require individual notification to those affected, in clear and simple terms. Separately, Gabon's Cybersecurity Law No. 027/2023 requires public administrations to report cybersecurity incidents to the competent authority as soon as they become aware of them.
